Operator
Good afternoon. This is the Chorus Call Conference Operator. Welcome, and thank you for joining the Generali Group Q1 2025 Results Presentation. As a reminder, all participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Should anyone need assistance during the conference call, they may signal an operator by pressing star and zero on their telephone. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Mr. Fabio Cleva, Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations. Please go ahead, sir.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Hello everyone, and thank you for joining our Q1 2025 Results Call. Here with us today, we have the Group General Manager Marco Sesana, the CEO of Insurance Giulio Terzariol, and the Group CFO Cristiano Borean. Before opening for Q&A, let me hand it over to Marco and Cristiano for some opening remarks.
Marco Sesana
Group General Manager, Generali Group
Hi everyone, good morning. Let me start by saying that these results mark the first step of Generali's next chapter within the Lifetime Partner 27: Driving Excellence plan presented in Venice in January. Soon after the Investor Day, the new strategy has been cascaded to the whole organization and operationalized through the setup of strategic programs. Implementation is focused to deliver seamless experience for our customers across channel and support to our advisors. Redesign of Group Standard on the first five critical touchpoints is already underway, and will be included into the whole business unit implementation plan by September. Other programs aim to secure our objective to profitably size P&C pocket of growth, such as SME and climate, and build a leadership position in protection, health, and accident, on top of transformation enablers such as shared service.
On AI and data, we are scaling the development of our 16 flagship AI applications, targeting over 60% adoption in the 10 largest business units already by the end of 2025. One example is our Geospatial Intelligence Platform, now active in four business units that will be live in 10 within the next nine months, boosting our risk monitoring and pricing in property underwriting. As you know, this is an ambitious plan where P&C is a key driver. Coming to our Q1 result, this shows that we are off to a good start, maintaining strong P&C momentum from the previous plan. Thanks to the action we implemented and the focus on the profit pool we have described during the Investor Day, the P&C top line is growing strongly at 8.6%. The vast majority of this is thanks to pricing, but volumes also are picking up in non-motor.
We expect this growth mix to evolve over the plan horizon, with the increasing multi-holding customers and our strategic focus on health and accident driving more volume growth over time. The top line dynamics of the Q1 reflect the fact that after two years of intense pruning, we have now a very clean portfolio, and we are therefore well positioned to reduce pruning while maintaining a strict underwriting discipline. Pricing continues to be conducive and in excess of risk premium across most of our geographies. The average annual premium is growing at a healthy rate of around 6%, and in motor, is now growing at around 8%. We implemented double-digit tariff increases in Germany at the January renewals. Pricing remained very good in Italy, and it has improved materially in Spain in the last six to nine months.
Let's look at margins. As you know, our target and our business steering are focused on the undiscounted combined ratio. However, I'm also very pleased that we achieve a reported combined ratio below 90. The combination of larger volume coming through and the sharp portfolio repricing in an environment where frequency is under control and claiming inflation has normalized makes me very confident about the future development. The improvement in the various technical metrics that we monitor at the business unit level gives me plenty of reason to expect a continuation of this positive underlying trend. We set ourselves an undiscounted combined ratio target of around 94.5% by the end of 2027, which also takes into account the volume growth we plan to achieve.
Clearly, the Q1 combined ratio also benefited from positively positive seasonality in terms of NatCat, with around EUR 50 million of claims in Q1 with a 0.6 percentage point impact on the combined ratio, while our NatCat budget for 2025 is at 2.8 percentage points. We have not experienced major events in Q2 so far. Let me share that according to our preliminary estimate, the group is expected to book around EUR 25 million of claims from the power outage in Spain in Q2. That exposure to liability contracts of our client in Spain is very much contained. Moving to life, let me remind you of our plan target together between EUR 25 and 30 billion of cumulative life net flows in our Lifetime Partner Plan 27.
The EUR 3 billion in Q1 is a very strong start. These flows are driven by our preferred line of business, so we had EUR 1.4 billion of net inflow in protection and health and EUR 1.2 billion in hybrid and unit-linked. These reflect the attractiveness of our product offering, the great job done by our agent and advisor, and the strong focus on customer experience. The numbers also demonstrate the gradual and ongoing improvement of lapses in Italy. Surrenders in Italy have not yet returned to the normal level, but they are on a good trajectory. Just to give you a sense, in Q1, surrenders were down 20% year-over-year in Italy. As Cristiano explained in the previous calls, our CSM now reflects a more conservative lapse hypothesis, so we feel comfortable with the whole development.
In this environment, we maintain a disciplined underwriting as our key principle. Let me share some quality data points. In Q1, over 81% of our new production has no guarantees. This is around 10 percentage points more than in Q1 of last year. The average guarantee on the guaranteed new business is almost 10 basis points lower than last year. The share of new production coming from capital-light products exceeds 89% compared to 85% in Q1 of 2024. The New Business Margin also increased by 26 basis points compared to last year. Please bear in mind that the lower interest rate environment compared to Q1 of 2024 has impacted the New Business Margin by 25 basis points. This means that the underlying margin of new business, excluding the market factor, has improved by over 50 basis points year-on-year.
As you know, we use rates of January, but please consider that if we measure our margin with the interest rate at the end of Q1, the number would be around 15 basis points higher. It is also important to note that the Q1 New Business Margin is impacted by the French protection business, without which the New Business Margin would be around 5.4%. Going forward for the next quarter, we target a New Business Margin between 5.25% and 5.75% under the current interest rate environment, and excluding the impact of large collective contracts that might blur the picture from quarter to quarter.
Now, let me close with a final word on investment and on asset allocation. The first four months of 2025 have seen a significant financial market volatility. However, equity and credit markets have recovered most of their early April moves. Thanks to our discipline and liability-driven asset allocation, we are well positioned to manage this environment, as also demonstrated by our resilient capital position as adverse market changes occur in April. This can also be observed by the fact that, excluding the volatile effect of Argentina, the current income has been increasing both in life and P&C, showing an improvement of the underlying profitability. Thanks for your attention, and let me now hand over to Cristiano.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali Group
Thank you, Marco. Hello everyone. Let me provide you some additional color on our Q1 financial performance to complement what you just heard on the underlying business trends. Starting with life, the CSM is up in the quarter with a normalized growth of 1.3%, also thanks to the positive seasonality of the new business at the beginning of the year. Most of the CSM walk is already available in the press release. Let me add for completeness that we recorded positive economic variances of EUR 57 million and negative operating variances of EUR 77 million, so the overall variances were broadly flat in the quarter. The economic variances benefited from higher interest rates and rising share prices in Europe, but this was partly compensated by the fact that non-European equities posted negative returns.
Less than 1/2 of our equity exposure in the general account is to listed equities, and around 1/2 of the non-listed equity portfolio is denominated in US dollars, which has depreciated versus the euro during the quarter, so this explains to you why we have enjoyed only moderate economic variances. Moving to operating variances, let me flag that they are entirely due to a specific one-off impact from a regulation change on the stamp duty on unit-linked reserves in Italy, which also impacted the Solvency II ratio. This is a one-and-done, with no additional impact in the future. This also means that we basically did not experience negative operating variances from lapses compared to around EUR 200 million experienced in Q1 2024.
The CSM release ratio of 2.5% slightly increased compared to 2024, reflecting, as I mentioned at the Investor Day, our conservative methodology on the EFA. Considering the release ratio mechanics of the year, which can also be influenced by changes in the underlying portfolio due to both enforced movements and new production, I expect our full-year 2025 CSM release ratio to be at the mid-high end of our 8% to 10% guidance. On the life operating investment result, we provided in the press release the key drivers of the year-on-year change. I'm happy to elaborate on them in the Q&A. Let me, however, confirm our guidance for a full-year 2025 life operating investment result of around EUR 900 million.
Moving to P&C, the key takeaway for me is that there is a powerful combination of top line growth coupled with margin expansion at the heart of what you see in the numbers we reported, with the P&C operating insurance service result growing EUR 180 million quarter-over-quarter, year-over-year. This is a growth rate of over 25%, and of course, we are very pleased by it, and it was achieved despite less discounting and conservative initial loss picks. Without these two effects, the attritional loss ratio would have improved even more. The direction of travel we see points to a nondiscounted combined ratio potentially below 95% in 2025, subject to, of course, the possible volatility stemming from the natural catastrophes. As we discussed previously, we changed the threshold to classify an event as NatCat from EUR 5 million to EUR 10 million.
At the risk of stating the obvious, this will lead to a bit more volatility in the attritional loss ratio from one quarter to the next. For example, in Q1, we had around EUR 20 million of cumulative claims that would have been classified as NatCat with the previous threshold, which have worsened the attritional loss ratio by almost 25 basis points. Going forward, it will be important to focus on the underlying business trends and to be able to dissect the signal from the noise in the quarterly moves, especially when it comes to the non-motor portfolio, where this slightly higher volatility is inherently more present. On prior year, some of you may ask why we had a prior year development above 2 percentage points in a quarter of benign NatCat. There are two very simple explanations.
First of all, in Q1, the lower revenue base amplifies the volatility of prior year development. Secondly, we had the release from some specific loss provision on large claims settled. Let me reiterate that we expect a 2 percentage point prior year development across the cycle, reflecting the prudence that we always exercise on the initial loss picks. However, you should not be surprised if there are quarters where this figure deviates from 2%, especially when the revenue base is smaller, like in Q1. Finally, in P&C, in the press release, we explained that excluding Argentina, the P&C investment income is up. Q1 bears the brunt of the Argentina effect because the improvement in inflation in Argentina accelerated in Q2 2024, and therefore, the differential between Q1 2024 and Q1 2025 is the highest.
This means that the remainder of the year will be better on this front. This is why I am confident to achieve the EUR 950 million guidance for the 2025 P&C investment result. Concerning holding another, I think that what will be important going forward is to consider that this segment will record some project costs related to the strategic initiatives we defined for the new plan, which will materialize primarily in 2025 in a range between EUR 25 and 15 million more compared to 2024. Moving to solvency, our capital generation is robust and has confirmed its resilience. The 210% Solvency II ratio reflects the strong capital generation, the diversified business model, and our disciplined asset allocation, all key strengths in a volatile environment. The market factors I mentioned for the CSM apply also here for the solvency.
I would like to emphasize that capital generation in Q1 was strong. We had 4 percentage points, but this includes the impact of around EUR 300 million from the buyback related to the Long-Term Incentive Plan. Just excluding the Long-Term Incentive Plan effect, our normalized capital generation would have been in the order of EUR 1.4 billion or close to 6 percentage points, a very healthy start of the year, reflecting the positive underlying dynamics across the business. As I did last year, let me also share the fact that as of today, we have received over 95% of the remittance we planned for 2025. As we always do, we schedule the collection of almost the entirety of the remittance to the parent company before we pay the dividend to the market.
To summarize, we started the Lifetime Partner 27: Driving Excellence Plan with a strong quarter: revenue growth, margin expansion, positive business dynamics that would continue to unfold across the group, and a resilient capital position. We manage the business for the long term with a focus on value creation for our investors, as also reflected in an adjusted earnings per share that is growing at 9.4 year-on-year, and with a relentless focus on keeping a strong nexus between the accounting result, the cash generation, and the solid capital position. Thank you for your attention. Operator, we are now ready for Q&A.
Operator
Thank you. This is the Chorus Call conference operator. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Anyone who wishes to ask a question may press star and one on their touch-tone telephone. To remove yourself from the question queue, please press star and two. Please pick up the receiver when asking questions. Anyone who has a question may press star and one at this time. The first question is from Andrew Baker, Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
Andrew Baker
Head of European Insurance Research, Goldman Sachs
Great. Thank you for taking my questions. The first one, just on the P&C combined ratio, so thank you for the additional detail on the cap volatility and the attritional. Are you able to give us any sense of the man-made losses in the quarter through the attritional, how this compared to last year? And then also how you're thinking about sort of man-made losses, or what your assumption is going forward that runs through the attritional? Secondly, I'm gonna give it a go, but we'll see what we get on this. Is there anything at all you're able to say on the Mediobanca bid for Banca Generali, whether that be your views, or failing that, sort of how we should think about any next steps in the process going forward? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you very much, Andrew. At this time, we have no further comments on the Banca Generali offer, while for the first question, I hand it over to Cristiano.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali Group
Yes. Good morning, Andrew. What we observed as a amount of effect in Q1 was an effect of a man-made of EUR 35 million compared to EUR 54 million in Q1 2024. As you know, man-made by nature is the real nitty-gritty job of insurance, should be part of the attritional and should be managed with a little bit of a pinch of salt because, clearly, they can move from one quarter to the other. What I can confirm is the strict underwriting discipline that has been made and the improved pricing capability, which is also managing it. What I can tell you that, going forward, the assumption clearly could be volatile, but we are talking of something on the order of 0.7, slightly less than 1 percentage point of impact with clearly a pinch of salt.
As you know, there is always a balance, and the fact that we are having initial loss picks prudent allows us to manage also this kind of volatility.
Andrew Baker
Head of European Insurance Research, Goldman Sachs
Great. Thank you so much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from Michael Huttner, Berenberg. Please go ahead.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Equity Research Analyst, Berenberg
Thank you so much. Well, I think the results are good, but I think your presentation was outstanding. It was almost like listening to some of the best analysts on the street, I mean, my colleagues. Really amazing. I'm struggling for questions, and I've got two. Pricing, could you give us a little bit more color? You said it's ahead of claims costs, which is lovely, but maybe a little bit more color, maybe by geography. Clearly, obviously, Germany, you're making a ton of money, but maybe you can speak a bit about some of the other main markets and that huge improvement in Spain, whether that can continue. You also highlighted the prudence in the loss picks. I just wanted to get a feel. My guess is that you fully offset the higher prior year development. I don't know. Any feel on that would be great. Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you very much, Michael. The first question is for Giulio, while the second one is for Cristiano.
Giulio Terzariol
CEO of Insurance, Generali Group
Hi, Michael. Thank you for the question. When we are focusing on motor in general, what we see on the motor line of business is the average earned premium is going up about 8%, and the risk premium is going up 3%. We have a spread between the two items of about 5 percentage points, which is a very good spread. This is explaining also the improvement that we see in our motor results, and we expect also to have improvement as we go further into 2025. When we look at the geography, I can tell you that, in general, we have a good pitch in all geographies. In Italy, we have an average earned premium, which is well above the risk premium substantially. Think about more than 5 percentage points of spread.
The same in Germany, where we have actually rate increases which are double-digit. There is a little bit more inflation in Germany compared to what we see in other geographies, but fundamentally, we have a very good spread between the average premium and the risk premium also in Germany. France is also a positive spread. Basically, I would tell you that across the board, we see a positive development. With regard to Spain, we have double-digit rate increases in Spain, and we have basically a spread to the risk premium, which is about 5 percentage points also there. What we saw in Spain, we've seen improvement in the motor combined ratio. The improvement has been a little bit clouded by some large losses, but we didn't see, for example, these large losses happening in April or in the first weeks of May.
From that point of view, we expect to see a further improvement in Spain. I would like to remind you that if you run the combined ratio of Spain, we are basically a 94 combined ratio. Overall, when you put together motor and non-motor, the Spanish business is performing anyway at a good level of combined ratio, but we think we can do even better. Overall, I would say it's a very strong picture. We are very pleased with the results, and also we know that there is still some improvement that we can realize in the course of 2025.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Equity Research Analyst, Berenberg
Fabulous. Thank you.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali Group
Good morning, Michael. Regarding the second point, I start with the end sentences. You have done a very educated guess, and I go to explain it, dedicating a few more topics out. Don't forget that on top of the 50 bps, there are 25 bps of the additional loss ratio impact from the change definition of the threshold. No, you should add the two together. On top of that, I would recall you that in the prior year development, maybe this is some, let's say, nitty-gritty point which could help anyone of you better understanding.
There is an asymmetric, like in the discounting, there is an asymmetric pattern throughout the year on the prior year release of the risk adjustment, which is higher in Q1 and goes down in Q2, which is counterbalanced and reflected in the loss ratio part, which is again with a higher risk adjustment negative impact, while it is in the prior year positive.
When looking, these quarters, especially if you don't look on a homogeneous quarter, Q1 versus this quarter, or you compare other quarters, this is an effect from two different quarters which are not the same, but if they are adjacent, has a 0.7 percentage point negative impact if you compare to the Q4, and of, for example, 2024, higher in the current year, okay, which shows you that it is important really to compare the quarter on the proper, open proper side these effects and the prudence I was mentioning. That's why our comments were particularly positive on what we have seen underlying and also with the prudence in the balance sheet.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Equity Research Analyst, Berenberg
Fabulous. Thank you very much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you, Michael. Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from Farooq Hanif at JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
Farooq Hanif
Head of European Insurance Equity Research, JPMorgan
Hi. Thanks very much. You talked about non-motor and going into accident and health that was mentioned by Marco at the beginning. Can you give a bit more detail on the products that you're really focusing on in non-motor, and are you able to give us, you know, a combined ratio comparison again between non-motor and motor to give us an idea of the mix effect there? Secondly, the discounting effect, for me anyway, was a little bit larger in Q1. Now, I know that, you know, that usually the effect is higher in the beginning and lower at the end. Do you have any change in view on the level of discounting effect for the full year? I guess the last point, question is, you know, we're seeing a lot of very good pricing, supporting the top line.
Given, you know, in retail markets, you know, these pricing cycles tend to be quite shallow, what's your kind of expectation about when you think the industry will see rate adequacy and when you think this kind of level of pricing is going to normalize in terms of the growth rate and pricing? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you very much, Farooq. The first question, I would say both for Marco and Giulio. Feel free to answer, both. Cristiano, the discounting question is for you, while the third one is for Giulio.
Marco Sesana
Group General Manager, Generali Group
Hi, Farooq. Thanks for all the question. I would say, I think that the most of our focus is on the, our traditional business. We know that we, everywhere, we are mainly a retail and SME group, mainly focus on, like in non-motor in Europe. Therefore, you should think our focus in enlarging the product density in a way in our customer base on these traditional type of products. We are talking about our, the protection for the family, the protection for the house, the protection for the small businesses, so these kind of things.
On top of this, you remember in Venice, we discussed some pocket of growth where we wanna really be focused. We discussed our focus on health. We discussed our focus on protecting, you know, the development of climate in the medium term. We discussed the focus on making sure that the SME have completely understood the risk that they have on cyber. I think overall, we are capturing these type of niches that are growing. Maybe health is not a niche because it's already very big, but it's still developing.
You should think our main business is developing on our core capabilities and core products. Just to give you an idea, our non-motor is still developing at a much better combined ratio, and I always have in mind attritional and discounted without NatCat. It's running at a better combined ratio than motor, clearly, about 62%, and our motor is still on the 70% range. This is the type of product we are focusing on.
Giulio Terzariol
CEO of Insurance, Generali Group
Yeah. Maybe I pick up the question about the outlook for retail. I would say the following. As I was saying before, for 2025, we still expect the earned premium to be ahead of the risk premium, and this is in motor. In non-motor, it's more or less a match. I would expect that as we go into 2026, most likely, the earned premium and the risk premium are going to be in line. From that point of view, in general, on the portfolio, I would expect that we are going to have this kind of situation. In some areas, we are still going to be able to get rate increases which are ahead of the risk premium. That's exactly in the portfolio, like Spain, where we need to get some additional traction.
What I would like anyway to highlight, if you take the numbers that we have right now for Q1, you basically normalize our combined ratio for NatCats. The combined ratio that we have in Q1 is 94.2%. Let's say it's 94.5% for the sake of argument. This combined ratio is, in my opinion, the right level, with quality at which we are running right now. Think about there can be still some improvement come in 2025. As we go into 2026, 2027, the improvement will not come mostly from pricing, but will come from the productivity that we want to put in place and also from the cost containment ratio. We are starting already from a level which is 94.5%.
Because of the pricing this year and because of other levels, we have still some room to go. You remember that our target for 2027 was of a combined ratio and discount to 94.5. From that point of view, I would say that we had a very good start, and we feel very well positioned to deliver on our 2020 or even overdeliver on our 2027 ambition.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali Group
Hi, Farooq. To complete, on the discounting effect, I would like to say that I agree, first of all, with you that the start of the year is bringing a slightly higher discounting. If we just measure not in percentage, but if we go on the range due to the production and the amount of rates, I was telling you last time we were in the EUR 550 to 600 million. I would say that we are in the EUR 600+ million range now with the actual rates, as of today.
Farooq Hanif
Head of European Insurance Equity Research, JPMorgan
That's excellent. Very brilliant. Thank you very much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you, Farooq. Next question, please.
Operator
Next question is from Stephen Hayward, HSBC. Please go ahead.
Stephen Hayward
Business Banking Manager, HSBC
Thank you very much. Just three hopefully quick questions for you. First one, on the asset management business, did you have any performance fees coming in the asset management business in Q1? I saw there was a lot for Banca Generali, but I just wanted to clarify for the asset management business. Secondly, I don't know if I missed this in your introduction, but do you have any full-year guidance for the investment result of the non-life business? Thirdly, you mentioned, obviously, surrender's not at a normal level in Italy yet. Are you expecting any potential variances or assumption changes to come later in the year for this?
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you very much, Stephen. I would say all three questions are for Cristiano.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali Group
Hello, Stephen. Q1, only on the asset management, excluding the EUR 34 million of performance fees of Banca Generali, posted EUR 2 million of performance fees in the asset management segment. The structure of the performance fees of the asset management is very different from the one of Banca Generali Wealth, it is totally skewed in the last part of the year where the vast majority comes in Q4, just for you to be aware of. This is performance fees. Other forms of non-regular fees, like transaction fees, can vary quarter to quarter according to the interaction, the most, let's say volatile are the performance one, which are skewed in Q4. The second question related to the investment result guidance for the year, yes. As I was saying, in the introductory speech, we confirm EUR 950 million. With this environment and interest rates, it is confirmed.
Third question, surrenders in Italy. We have experienced, as Marco was saying, a reduction of surrender in amount, by 20%, which is in line from what now has been put in our CSM as well as in our new business value hypothesis, which were accordingly changed at the same logic of the CSM stock, which means that there are no deviations from what we have projected and budgeted.
Stephen Hayward
Business Banking Manager, HSBC
Excellent. Thank you very much. Good luck.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you, Stephen. Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from Fahad Changazi, Kepler Cheuvreux. Please go ahead.
Fahad Changazi
Equity Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux
Oh, hello. Thank you for taking my questions. Just very quick follow-ups. Regarding the New Business Margin guidance for the subsequent quarters of 5.25% to 5.75%, if this lapse is improved further, presumably, that will sort of make us go to higher end of the range. Could you also comment on what's happening with your commercial incentives in Italy, and how we should think about that as we go through the year? Another question, please, is on the Natixis JV. Can you give any detail on the process and timeline of the Italian government's review? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you very much, Fahad. The first question on the New Business Margin and commercial incentives is for Marco, while, Fahad, at this stage, there are no updates that we give regarding Natixis JV.
Marco Sesana
Group General Manager, Generali Group
Let me, maybe, build on the, on the topic of lapses and guidance on New Business Margin. As I said at the beginning, lapses are going down, not at the level like, let's say, at 2020, but there are, like, business reasons for this. First, the interest rate environment is completely different, and, therefore, this has an impact on the type of lapses that we see. Second, also, you know, the more we go on, the more the type of business we are selling matters because we have a much more hybrid stock of asset under management that we sold in the past. Therefore, we do see that this has naturally a little bit more lapse even because, you know, the type of product is a whole life.
In the end, it needs to have this kind of trend. We don't expect that this is going back to like 2020 number, but I would say the trend that we see is completely in line with what we expected during the year. I think we can confirm the guidance that we give in 5.25 to 5.75. The other topic was on commercial incentive, right? Commercial incentive, as much as we are normalizing the situation, we are scaling back commercial incentive, and we are focusing a little bit more on quality volume coming in. This is the type of movement that we see in the Italian business at the moment.
Fahad Changazi
Equity Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux
Okay. That's great. Thank you.
Marco Sesana
Group General Manager, Generali Group
Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you, Fahad. Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from William Hawkins, KBW. Please go ahead.
William Hawkins [Director of Research
Europe] (KBW)
Morning, all. Sorry, I've got three. I hope they're quick. Can you just help me understand a bit more the walk towards the EUR 950 million non-life investment income guidance, please? I'd be keen to know the Argentinian impact on the two Q1 figures. More importantly, if I just take 164 and multiply it by 4, that's EUR 650 million, which is EUR 300 million short of the guidance you're giving. If you could help me understand how we accelerate to the end of the year, please. Secondly, on the PVNBP that declined to EUR 17.3 billion this Q1, if we exclude China and France, what was the growth rate in that number, please? Can we assume that that growth rate continues for the rest of the year?
Then lastly, sorry if I'm being a nerd, but the balancing item between, in life, the balancing item between the CSM release and the insurance service result seemed unusually positive this quarter. My assumption is that all the other things, like risk adjustment, loss component, and the rest of it, nets out to zero as a normal assumption. Is that correct? If it's not correct, can you just tell me, you know, how positive or how negative is all the other stuff? Cause it felt to me like it was unusually positive this quarter. Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you very much, William. All three questions are for Cristiano.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali Group
I start with the third one, which is the easiest, and it is concentrated in the simple fact that we had a reversal of loss component because of the higher interest rates environment, which was accounting for EUR 47 million. We have positive experience variance, mainly related to the PAA business in our French activities of something of the order of EUR 29 million. These are the drivers which were bringing the support. The decline of PVNBP, if we exclude China, the China impact out of that, would have been something like +5% number, I would say, doing it by heart. The walk from EUR 950 million in Q1, we posted in the P&C investment result something of the order of EUR 164 million.
Don't forget that this is the joint effect of operating investment income and finance expenses. Excluding Argentina, this number would have been broadly the same because the effect on the investment result and the finance expenses would have gone down. To have a clean round rate, you should take the EUR 326 million of operating investment income without Argentina, multiply it times 4, add EUR 100 million of the operating investment income that we are expecting from Argentina, and add the EUR 150 million dividend distribution, subtracting EUR 600 million of EFIs. If you do that, math is not wrong to bring me to the EUR 950 guidance.
William Hawkins [Director of Research
Europe] (KBW)
That's fantastic. Thank you very much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thanks to you, William. Next question, please.
Operator
As a reminder, if you wish to register for a question, please press star and one on your telephone. The next question is a follow-up from Michael Huttner, Berenberg. Please go ahead.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Equity Research Analyst, Berenberg
Fantastic. I forgot my way. I like asking about cash. Can you.. I was just looking at your presentation. Over EUR 11 billion is the target for the full-year plan, cumulative net holding cash flow. I just wondered if you can give us a feel for where we are relative to the plan and also what kind of sort of level of one-offs, I know you talked about it in Venice, but also the full year, but it'd be a reminder. It'd be lovely. Thank you.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali Group
Yes, William. We are exactly in line with the plan, especially because, you know, when we presented the 2025, at end of January 2025, the Strategic Plan 2025/2027, the decision on the remittance for 2025 was taken. There was much less uncertainty. I would expect potentially some positive second-order effect on the year coming from better than projected result, which will come. That's why we, I'm saying that we are above 95 but not at 100 and some small pieces.
Saying, projecting farther, what pleased me in the results I've seen today, and I think in all what Marco and Giulio are telling you from the underlying business, is that these results, even in the life component you've seen, they are more and more driven by cash, component, and elements because if you just take the P&C, the discounting cancels out with the unwinding of the EFI, and you are really posting an improvement which is fully driven by cash elements. This is a very solid mix to bring you a more than EUR 11 billion net holding EFI cash flow cumulated.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Equity Research Analyst, Berenberg
Fantastic. Thank you very much.
Operator
Gentlemen, there are no more questions registered at this time. I turn the conference back to you for any closing remarks.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali Group
Thank you, operator. This concludes our Q1 2025 results call. Thanks everyone, for dialing in, and, of course, the IR team remains at your full disposal for any follow-up. Enjoy the rest of your day. Goodbye.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for joining. The conference is now over, and you may disconnect your telephones.

content.text:
Operator
Good afternoon. This is the conference operator. Welcome, and thank you for joining the Generali Group Full Year 2024 Results Presentation. As a reminder, all participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Should anyone need assistance during the conference call, they may signal an operator by pressing star and zero on their telephone. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Mr. Fabio Cleva, Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations. Please go ahead, sir.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining our full year 2024 results call. Here with us today, we have our Group CEO, Philippe Donnet, the General Manager, Marco Sesana, the CEO of Insurance, Giulio Terzariol, and the Group CFO, Cristiano Borean. Before opening for Q&A, let me hand it over to Philippe for some opening remarks.
Philippe Donnet
Group CEO, Generali
Thank you, Fabio. Good morning, and thank you for attending our full year 2024 results call for which I'm joined by Cristiano, Giulio, and Marco. Before we open the Q&A, let me share a few key remarks with you. These results mark the conclusion of our Lifetime Partner 24: Driving Growth plan, and we are proud to have over-delivered against all financial targets. It is the third consecutive strategic plan we have successfully completed, and our 2024 results further confirm our group is the strongest it has ever been. The operating result at EUR 7.3 billion, and the adjusted net result at EUR 3.8 billion for the full year are new record highs, and they have been achieved thanks to the very positive contribution from all business segments.
When we presented our full year 2023 results, I stressed that the return to positive net collection would be one of our priorities. In Life, net inflows at year-end 2024 were close to EUR 10 billion. This great achievement, which is unparalleled in the industry, was made possible by our powerful distribution force. Therefore, let me thank our agents and advisors for their excellent work. These net inflows were entirely driven by protection and unit-linked lines. Our continued focus on underwriting discipline and in-force management has resulted in a further increase in the share of life reserves related to capital light products, reaching 71% at year-end. In Property and casualty, the 7.7% increase in gross written premiums was driven by the positive performance of both motor and non-motor lines, which grew in all the main markets where we operate.
Our tariff strengthening measures also continued to be effective throughout the year. This is also reflected in our improved undiscounted combined ratio below 96% in line with our guidance, even when considering the EUR 1.2 billion effect of natural catastrophes. The underlying trend showcases the ability of the team to successfully deliver. Our undiscounted loss ratio, excluding nat cat in prior years, shows at 1.4 percentage point improvement. This is by far the best in the industry, and it would be close to 2 points with the same perimeter as 2023 excluding Liberty Seguros. Giulio told you at our Investor Day, we are strongly focused on continued improvement in technical excellence, and this performance shows we are starting the new plan with a very positive momentum also on this front.
Looking ahead, we are convinced that the key trends we shared on that occasion will create significant profitable growth opportunities for Generali. In line with the increasing demand from customers, premiums related to protection, health, and accident continued to accelerate and now account for around 22% of the group's overall gross written premiums. This segment is highly profitable, and it is central to our plan to increase the number of multi-holding customers. We have three key strengths that will ensure we achieve this. First, the best relationship net promoter score among our main peers. Second, a modular product offering to respond to customer needs. And third, a highly effective distribution platform boosted by enhanced usage of data and artificial intelligence. Proprietary distribution is an important cornerstone of our offering. We distribute over half of the policies through agents, almost double the average in the industry.
When interest rates decline, our agents enable us to transform our live book. When lapses increase, they enabled us to perform better than the market. As Marco highlighted in his presentation in Venice, our agents are fundamental in capturing growth across our preferred lines of business. Moving to asset and wealth management, the group's total assets under management reached EUR 863 billion, growing by 32%, thanks to the positive net inflows and the consolidation of Conning Holdings Limited. The operating result of this segment grew by almost 23% to EUR 1.2 billion. At the Investor Day, Woody explained the importance of having an integrated offering between our large life insurance book and our strengthened asset management platform. Fully leveraging this relationship is key for us.
When this management team took over the helm of the group, remittances from subsidiaries were around EUR 2.4 billion. In 2024, they reached EUR 4.5 billion, contributing to the highest net holding cash flow we have ever reported at EUR 3.8 billion. The relentless focus on cash and capital optimization has been one of Cristiano's priorities in the past six years as Group CFO, and it will continue to be an essential part of our focus on growing shareholder remuneration.
Thanks to this, healthy cash flow generation, a solid capital position with a 220% Solvency II ratio, and the underlying growth of the business, we will propose at the next annual general meeting a dividend per share of EUR 1.43, up by almost 12% year-over-year, as well as a EUR 500 million share buyback to be launched this year subject to regulatory approval. Finally, I would like to mention the further significant progress we made as a responsible investor, insurer, employer, and corporate citizen. This will continue with Lifetime Partner 27: Driving Excellence, which has sustainability as one of its three key foundations. In conclusion, our 2024 financial performance is the result of our hard work across the last three strategic cycles, and we are now already focusing on the delivery of our new plan.
We have committed once more to very ambitious targets, and we have everything it takes to succeed and to keep creating sustainable value for all stakeholders while driving excellence in everything we do. Before we open our Q&A, let me just remind you that we will be hosting our annual general meeting on 24 April 2024 in Trieste. I look forward to seeing you there, and I thank you very much for your attention. Operator, we are now ready to take questions on our 2024 results.
Operator
Thank you. This is the Chorus Call conference operator. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Anyone who wishes to ask a question may press star and one on their touchtone telephone. To remove yourself from the question queue, please press star and two. We kindly ask to use handsets when asking questions. Anyone who has a question may press star and one at this time. The first question is from David Barma, Bank of America. Please go ahead.
David Barma
VP of Equity Research, Bank of America
Good morning. Thank you for taking my questions. The first one is on the very good performance in P&C in Q4. You've improved your undiscounted current year loss ratio by around 1.6% in Q4 compared to the nine months, which was the starting point of the new cycle. Actually we're even closer to the 2.5% if we account for the fact that manmade losses were higher in Q4. That's better than your target for the next three years. I realize it's only one quarter, but I would expect the underlying profitability to further improve given the good trajectory of pricing for at least 2025.
Can you talk a little bit about this and the Q4 performance versus the improvement expected over the next three years? That's my first question. Staying on P&C and motor lines specifically, would you say most of the pruning is now behind, especially in Italy, and we can now start seeing a bit more volume growth in 2025? Lastly on cash, the CMD, I think you suggested you'd get around EUR 400 million of remittances from management actions in 2025. But I would have thought the Liberty Seguros excess capital and the measures you've taken with Allianz and Genertel would give you more than that already.
Can you please come back on the management actions that are expected to come through in 2025, please? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, David. The first two questions are for Giulio, while the third one is for Cristiano.
Giulio Terzariol
CEO of Insurance, Generali
No, thank you, David, for the questions. You know, on the Q4 development, I will never read too much into a slice besides the fact that this gives you clearly the idea of the confidence that we have as we go also into 2025. Why I'm saying you shouldn't read too much into a slice of a quarter, because at the end of the year, you have always the validation of all the assumptions that you have, you know. In that sense, you get a little bit of a catch-up effect from an accounting point of view in the quarter. Clearly when you see a strong ending, this means that we have a lot of quality in our numbers.
If you look at where we are standing right now in motor, the undiscounted combined ratio is 98, so that's a very strong basis. As we think about also 2025, we still expect to see rate increases on top of the inflation. From that point of view, there is room to do even better. To your specific question about pruning, I would say we have limited situation where we really need a pruning, and a situation like that might be Generali in Italy. In some geography, more than pruning, we still need to get some additional pricing. I'm thinking about Spain and Portugal.
Fundamentally, we have a strong performance already now, and we expect also to see some further improvement from a very good level in 2025 and beyond. Also, Non-Motor, we are running at a good combined ratio, especially if we adjust for the net CAT impact, and we normalize for that. Clearly on Non-Motor, we need to be always a little bit cautious because assuming that the net CAT budget is going to be lower is an assumption. I think we are well positioned also if we are going to see more elevated net CAT compared to our assumption.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hi, David. Going to the 2025 expectation, I think that what is important to keep in mind is what I was telling you at Investor Day, where basically the 2024 has been a special year with the EUR 400 million coming from Italy and EUR 200 million coming from Austria. In 2025, you should expect something like capital management action of the order of, I would say, EUR 400 to EUR 450 million, including all the action which will entail, again, Italy, as we were highlighting.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from Andrew Baker, Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.
Andrew Baker
Head of European Insurance Research, Goldman Sachs
Hi. Thank you for taking my questions. The first one is on just the CSM operating variances. Are you able to give just a little bit more color on the model refinements that you did in France, Germany, and Asia? Also related to that, what should we think or how should we think about the 2025 operating variance coming through on the lapse side from your methodology change? Any guidance there would be helpful. Secondly, your Q4 life new business margin was sequentially higher than Q3, which is more positive than you guided at the time. Just curious what drove this sequential development versus what you had expected. Also, are you able to give the new business value for 2024, what it would have been under your new definition going forward? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Andrew. The first and the third question are for Cristiano, while the second one on the new business margin in Q4 is for Marco.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Yeah, for sure. Hello, Andrew. On top of the lapses effect, which accounts for the EUR 1.1 billion over the total EUR 1.4 billion, the EUR 0.3 billion effect of the last quarter, which are not related to the lapses on refinement, are mainly model changes in France related to the way it is treated the movement between unit-linked payout and multi-hybrid product, while some change in assumption of expense review on Germany and more negative development of morbidity assumption in China. These are the main three drivers which all of them, the three of them summed up to around the EUR 0.3 billion.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Marco, the new business margin.
Marco Sesana
General Manager, Generali
Yeah. I think the development that we are seeing on the new business margin overall is in line with what we pointed out as a guidance into the beginning of the year. We said we were seeing an improvement of the new business margin across the different quarters. We are coming to the level where we expect it to be. In particular, you know that we have always said that we would have done, you know, trade-off versus, you know, on volume versus margins, and, you know, scaling back gradually over the next months, the commercial incentive that we had to improve our collection, and that's what we did. We are at the level where we expect it to be. Again, going maybe I think it's useful also to look forward.
What we expect for the next few months, we do expect this level of new business margin going forward. Clearly we will need to be also tactical and gradually understanding the macro situation on the interest rate to understand when to cut back more on the commercial action and having a good creation of value. Because just want to remind that everything is done to create more value overall. New business margin, new business volume are on, in that line. Cristiano.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Yes. Andrew, just to complete on the 2025 guidance, which on the CSM I did mention before.
After having made all these changes in the lapses hypothesis, we expect a much more stable development of the operating variances next year, which will be materially decreasing down to very minor effect. Just to clarify. On the third question on what would be the new business value, new business margin under the new definition, which we discussed also during the investor day, you should read the new business value as EUR 3 billion, so basically EUR 0.7 billion more with the new definition. The new business margin would increase by 80 basis points to 5.4%, hinting into an improvement of 15 to 20 basis points as a margin moving into 2025.
Andrew Baker
Head of European Insurance Research, Goldman Sachs
Very helpful. Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thanks to you, Andrew. Next question please.
Operator
The next question is from Michael Huttner, Berenberg. Please go ahead.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Analyst, Berenberg
Fantastic. Thank you. Just congratulations. Three cycles in a row is amazing. I have three really live questions. The first is a bit continuation of one of the previous questions, the cash outlook. I noticed that in 2024 you had quite a big number from, or quite a big increase from others. I just wondered what is that and how much more we could get. Also, I think you had the question that there was Liberty, there's EUR 300 million left there, whether that's included in the management actions you cited. The second is also on cash Switzerland. I remember you said MAMA takes back, and I wondered, is this already starting in 2025?
The third question is something I think you said, Philippe, in an interview that you're going to be buying more Italian government bonds. I just wondered if you can maybe explain your thinking there. Thanks a lot.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Michael. The first question and the second one on cash are for Cristiano, while of course the BTP one is for Philippe.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hi, Michael. So, the increase in the other remittance of 2024 should be considered also with some, for example, one-off contribution from M&A initiatives like some dividends we received from Malaysia, if I take the example in 2024. On the other hand, don't forget that also we had in 2023 some high dividends coming from the asset management because of the preparation for the Conning deal. Going to Liberty, is it included in the management action of the CFO? Yes. They are there.
We are already starting to get the cash back in Q1 2025 from Liberty as a first piece, and the second one is throughout the year. On Switzerland, is it already starting in 2025, the remittance? The answer is we are not. We are completing a final step because the very healthy situation of the life company. Be aware that we are slightly above 250% of Swiss Solvency Test ratio for the year-end 2024. Everything is set in line to prepare, but we agreed to have a 2025 yearly stabilization and understanding on the full sensitivities with all the numbers to get starting from 2026. As you mentioned, what Mama gives, Mama will start to ask.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Analyst, Berenberg
Thank you.
Philippe Donnet
Group CEO, Generali
Hello, Michael. As you know, our BTP portfolio is linked to our insurance liabilities in Italy, and it will always be the case. As of 31 December 2024, the group exposure to government bonds was EUR 35.6 billion, compared to EUR 38.5 billion by the end of 2023, and almost entirely in support to our Italian life business. This also includes EUR 5.6 billion held by Banca Generali.
As an Italian group with a significant and profitable life insurance business in Italy, BTPs naturally are an important part of our investment allocation. As a result of the developments in the markets and the positive, the very positive net inflows for 2024, we are looking into increasing our purchases of BTPs, obviously, in line with our investment policy and with our risk tolerance.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Analyst, Berenberg
Brilliant. Thank you. Thank you very much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thanks to you, Michael. Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from Farooq Hanif at J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.
Farooq Hanif
Head of European Insurance Equity Research, JPMorgan
Hi, everybody. Thank you so much. Could you please talk about the jump in the life investment margin? Kind of any one-offs that were in 2024 that we need to take out, and also, you had a very good investment income, too, in P&C. So just comment, I guess, around the sustainability of that given current macro. Second question on margins. I mean, when you adjust for your new approach, you're already quite close to your 6% new business margin target in life. So I was wondering what the path to get there looks like. I mean, is it quite an easy jump from now, for example, in 2025 or 2026 to, you know, to get there more quickly?
In that context, I notice there's a big jump in the margin in CEE. You comment on it in your slides, but if you could give us more details about what's going on there, that'd be really helpful. Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Farooq. The first question is for Cristiano, while the second one is for Giulio.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hello, Farooq. I think you're referring to the life investment result when you call the margin.
Farooq Hanif
Head of European Insurance Equity Research, JPMorgan
Yeah.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
The effect actually, if I just check, versus the 2023 number in the last quarter, there has been a slow reduction versus the 2023, as you've seen, because we had lower rates. There is an effect, which is related to the fact that we are locally adopting in China, IFRS 17 locally, which entails to have a single rate to be applied, which has slightly higher interest rates, which are unwound than in the IFE, which has some more negative impact going forward, which are clearly counterbalanced element of the value on the other side.
There has also been an effect, which is a shift from the excess capital from the life shareholder equity to P&C shareholder equity in Argentina, and that shift weighs EUR 30 million. All in all, let me tell you that the investment result for 2024 should be read for a guidance of 2025 of around EUR 900 million, including this effect of what I was mentioning you, higher IFE stemming from this changing curve also in China. This is what I would mention on that. On the P&C side, I think that we should consider as the shift I was mentioning from life to P&C will be recurring for the P&C extra return from Argentina.
I mentioned before that already at Investor Day that we should not take into account this volatility stemming from the Argentina side. In a world which last year was quite positive, the contribution, so I think that a run rate to be projected for 2025 around the EUR 950 million is a good conservative estimation you should plug in with this level of also lower interest rates also in the cash return.
Farooq Hanif
Head of European Insurance Equity Research, JPMorgan
Thank you.
Giulio Terzariol
CEO of Insurance, Generali
We can go into the life side. Maybe first I answer your question about the jump in the new business margin in Eastern Europe. That's first of all, keep in mind that in Eastern Europe, about three-quarters of our premiums are protection. That's a very profitable business. When rates are going down, the new business margin protection goes up. We had also some change in operating assumptions. That's a positive. We also have less inflation on the Spanish side, and that's also contributed to a better new business margin. We are very pleased with the level. We are pleased with improvement, and also it's very important, we think we can keep this level moving forward. Clearly we're going to push especially on the protection element in Eastern Europe.
Now, on your question, a broader scope, I would say that, going from the 5.4% that Cristiano was referring before to the 6% that we put into our strategic plan, it's not super easy. We need to work on that. You need to keep in mind that our new business margin is already at a high level. We are starting generally from a high level, point of view. It's one of the best new business margin you can see clearly in the industry. From that point of view, there is some work that we need to do in order to go from the 5.4% to the 6%.
One element is going to be the mix, because over the plan horizon, we expect to see more protection compared, for example, to savings, and automatically this should push the new business margin up. Fundamentally, we have a plan how to get there. If you ask me it's a given, I will say it's not a given. We need clearly to work over the next three years on that. The good part of the story, we have a strong distribution. From that point of view, you know, we can really control our destiny, but there is some work to do on this one.
Farooq Hanif
Head of European Insurance Equity Research, JPMorgan
Thank you very much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thanks to you. Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from Iain Pearce, BNP Paribas Exane. Please go ahead.
Iain Pearce
Executive Director of Insurance Equity Research, Exane BNP Paribas
Hi. Thanks for taking my questions. Two just around the motor business. The first one is on the 98% full year combined ratio, which is a bit better than what I thought you spoke about at the investor day. Just trying to understand if there's anything sort of one-off or some favorable experience, favorable PYD in there, or if you think the 98% is a true sort of underlying level and a good starting point for the 2027 plan. The second one is just on the motor businesses in France and Italy. It looks like they're growing below the level of rate increase that or average premium increase you would have been achieving in 2024.
You flagged some challenges around Genertel in Italy. I wonder if you could firstly just elaborate on why that's so challenging in the direct segment, and if you expect those businesses to return to above premium increase growth in 2024 in France and Italy. That'd be 2025, sorry, in France and Italy. If you can elaborate on that'd be great. Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Ian. Both questions are for Giulio.
Giulio Terzariol
CEO of Insurance, Generali
Okay. Starting from motor. Yeah, I would say the 98% is a good proxy for the starting point. From that point of view, there are no special one-offs justifying the 98%. From that point of view, you can take this as a reference. Next year, considering the rate increases that we have, which are on top of inflation, we should expect the 98% to be even lower. We feel very good about the work that we have done on the motor side. Just maybe two question marks is Spain and Portugal, and not because we are not taking actions, but because in Spain and Portugal, we are seeing inflation to be more persistent compared to other geographies.
A positive thing that we are seeing on the motor side is, inflation's coming down a bit, but especially we see lower frequency basically across the board. From that point of view, we might expect also to see lower frequency continuing into the next year. Fundamentally is a strong business right now with a good performance and also with potential for further improvement. On France and Italy, I would say in Italy the situation is being especially driven by Genertel, but also aside Genertel, we are not necessarily increasing in motor the number of policy. This happens more in non-motor. Think about Italy, Genertel is clearly taking down if you want the number of risks.
On the non-Genertel side, there is a slight negative, but this is a reflection, clearly the effort that we are putting to get to the good combination motor that you're seeing. On France, there was more of a pruning in motor, especially at the beginning of the year. Now we are taking some corrective action also because the performance is very good. I would expect that as we go into 2025, we are going to see a higher growth, if you want, or less of a pruning effect in motor compared to what you saw in the course of 2024.
Iain Pearce
Executive Director of Insurance Equity Research, Exane BNP Paribas
Perfect. Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you, Iain. Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from William Hawkins, KBW. Please go ahead.
William Hawkins
Director of European Insurance Research, KBW
Hi, guys. Thank you very much. I'm just coming back on some of your answers you've already given, so forgive me, please. Your life investment results, the outlook, did I hear you say EUR 900 million for 2025? Because that feels very low relative to the EUR 943 million for a business that should be growing. Just could you repeat what you said about the outlook for the life investment result, please? Then secondly, you've already been very kind on the detail of the new business margin, but the specific impact of the commercial initiatives, they dragged 50 basis points last year. What are you expecting the drag is gonna be in 2025?
Do we keep that sort of pari passu with the new methodology, or is there, you know, some reason why it might change in the new methodology? Then lastly please, I'm sorry to have begun because I was trying to type while you were talking. The higher exposure to BTPs, are you simply saying that your business will be bigger, so of course you're gonna own more BTPs? Or is there actually a suggestion that your economic weighting towards BTPs could be rising? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, William. The first question is for Cristiano, the second one is for Marco, and the third one is for Giulio, and of course, Marco, if you want to comment.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hi, William. Let me remind you, when we talk about life investment result, we are talking about the non-VFA business. Non-VFA business is clearly related to some specific business we are having, but there are also running off pieces of our portfolio. I'm thinking about the Czech Republic portfolio, which has a run-off nature out of that on top. On top of what I told you before. We stick to this number. I said always when this estimation are given, we try to make a conservative estimation out of that.
I think the EUR 900 million is a good reflection also of this due to the fact that the shift from the excess capital in Argentina from life to P&C itself is only, I mean, EUR 30 million as a weight on a yearly basis. This is the outlook. Don't forget that what I was mentioning about the non-VFA other part of the growth with the Asian change in China, which is having higher unwinding of the embedded cost and guarantees out of that.
Marco Sesana
General Manager, Generali
Yeah. Hi, William. Just to maybe go back to what we intend to do in 2025, clearly, as you know, we expect, you know, all the external environment to be a little bit volatile. We are planning to reduce those commercial incentive. We will look into quarter by quarter how much it's possible to do. We wanna make sure that we are stronger on the value creation, therefore, we will see how that can be reduced. We do expect to reduce it. By the way, these will stay broadly unchanged with the new methodology, so this number.
We do expect them to reduce it, but we are gonna be tactical, you know, understanding how much is the environment changing and how much we can do.
Philippe Donnet
Group CEO, Generali
Yes. Hello, William. On the BTPs, I said that the exposure has been decreasing significantly between the end of 2023 and the end of 2024, from EUR 38.5 billion down to EUR 35.6 billion. Marco Sesana

We would like to slightly increase and tactically increase, but over time, our exposure to private markets, so private equity, private credit in particular. That direction is unchanged. Clearly, you know, we have defined a plan horizon direction. Clearly, this is gonna change, you know, as long as, you know, in line with the external condition, this might be fine-tuned or tweaked a little bit over the different quarters.

William Hawkins
Director of European Insurance Research, KBW
It's helpful color. Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you, William. Next question, please.

Gianluca Ferrari
Equity Analyst, Mediobanca
Yes. Hi, good afternoon, everyone. Three for me, please. The first one is credit spread sensitivities. I noticed they went up quite materially, particularly on the CSM. Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Gianluca. The first two questions on the CSM are for Cristiano, while the third one is for Philippe.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hi, Gianluca.
Gianluca Ferrari
Equity Analyst, Mediobanca
Ciao.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Credit spreads, sensitivities, I think what matters most is no specific topic, honestly, out of that about the rating of the book. I think what is also important to keep in mind is more the government spread sensitivities which we experience in the CSM, which I think you have seen brought down a material EUR 0.3 to 0.4 billion CSM effect only in the quarter. Reminding you that our Swiss business, what is left there, notwithstanding a good ALM, has also a long duration.
The nature of the government sensitivity to swap spread is extremely high due to the dependency on the matching, which is a peculiar feature, if you allow me, both of the IFRS 17 and as well as of the solvency that we are all experiencing in this period when there is the full decoupling between the government bond movement in the rates versus the swap rate, which is a collateralized baseline rate way we are observing this deviation. I think these are the main explanation also going there.
Gianluca Ferrari
Equity Analyst, Mediobanca
Thank you.
Philippe Donnet
Group CEO, Generali
Hello, Gianluca. On your third question, let me remind you first that in our new plan, we have been very clear on our very strict approach and discipline on M&A, as we will benchmark any opportunity against share buybacks. Gianluca Ferrari
Equity Analyst, Mediobanca
Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you, Gianluca. Next question, please.

The next question is from Hadley Cohen, Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.
Hadley Cohen
Head of European Insurance Research, Morgan Stanley
Hi. Morning, everyone. Thanks very much. Two questions, please. Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Hadley. Maybe we start with the second question with Giulio on the Q1 development in Life, while the first question clearly is for Cristiano.
Giulio Terzariol
CEO of Insurance, Generali
From a flow situation in general, we see clearly positive flows into the beginning of the year. Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Yeah. Hi, Hadley. So, regarding redemption for Life, we are expecting something around 3.2% in 2025. While as an average, sorry, for the group, which is split between 3.5% in Life and 2.2% in P&C. These are the two main drivers you should focus on more than the average per se.
Hadley Cohen
Head of European Insurance Research, Morgan Stanley
Perfect. Thanks very much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Hadley. Next question, please.
Operator
The next question is from Fahad Changazi, Kepler Cheuvreux. Please go ahead.
Fahad Changazi
Equity Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux
Yeah. Thank you for taking my question. Two questions, please. It sounds promising on the underlying loss ratio, but could you comment on the expense ratio for 2025? I think given a change in mix in non-motor versus motor, there was going to be an impact on acquisition costs. Is this still the case for 2025, given we're expecting some growth in motor premiums? A second question on Solvency II life in-force returns, could you give some indication on how that will develop in 2025 given the lower swap rates? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Fahad. Both questions are for Cristiano.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Yeah. First of all, when we look at the expense ratio development in the year, don't forget that this year was specifically affected by the so-called Liberty effect. If I just take out the Liberty effect, the expense ratio of the year would be reducing by 0.1%, so 10 basis points versus the 30 basis points we are showing. That is a better starting point to project starting from next year, which would keep, in any case, a double effect, which we were highlighting already in the Investor Day.
Don't forget that, in the 2025-2027 plan, we are driving through higher amount of non-motor component growth in high growth countries, like, Asian countries like India, where there is a higher acquisition cost, together with higher acquisition cost of non-motor per se, which in the mix is not bringing a material change to what you should expect in 2025 versus what we had in 2024 adjusted for the Liberty. Fahad Changazi
Equity Analyst, Kepler Cheuvreux
That's great. Thank you very much.

Thank you very much, Rhea. The first question is for Giulio, while the second question is for Cristiano.
Giulio Terzariol
CEO of Insurance, Generali
The first question, it's always challenging to give an exact split. I would say anyway, the majority of the improvement is coming from clearly the tariff increases that we're pushing through. For example, when we speak about frequency, which is reducing, this might be a consequence of the general trend, but also of the underwriting actions that we are taking. Doing the split is always a little bit of a complex exercise. For the time being, I would say the majority of the improvement is coming from the rate environment. I would expect this to be the case also as we go into 2025.
Clearly, as we think about the last part of the improvement we want to get, this is coming most likely not from rate increases over inflation, but more from the pruning, the claims initiative that were put in place. As I think about the timeline, think about price strength is right now the major driver of improvement. When we think about the planning at the back end of the plan, clearly the initiatives that we have put in place are going to help us to get to our targets. That's it, yeah, on this one.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hi Rhea. For the second question, first of all, when we comment within the other business, it is right because in the element you should always take into account, but you should add the consolidation adjustment effect of the intra-group dividend, the one which this year created the EUR 60 million more consolidation adjustment because there were EUR 60 million less intra-group dividend which were taken down. Projecting that, the 2024 is a good run rate number more than the 2023, which was positively impacted by some excess capital repatriation on, for example, the asset management component I was mentioning before to prepare for the Conning deal.
I would say 2024 is a much more representative number also because we have minor businesses inside which are interest rate dependent, and the 2024 interest rate environment is much more in line with the one observed in 2025 versus the one in 2023, which was much higher and was potentially having a small benefit out of that.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Next question, please.

The next question is a follow-up from Michael Huttner, Berenberg. Please go ahead.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Analyst, Berenberg
I'm very lucky, so I'll keep it really brief. Just one question. The capital generation, an amazing number, EUR 4.8 billion, 21%, for a group growing as fast as you, that's an extraordinary number. You're well ahead of the target to get to EUR 14 billion in next three-year plan. Can you explain a little bit what's driving this huge beat? Thank you.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hi, Michael. Clearly, as we were already discussing during the investor day, we confirm that our view on the capital generation takes also into account some margin of prudence because of the adverse potential scenario we can always face, you know. By the way, I think the EUR 4.5 billion is a good starting point onto which project. Clearly the improvement that we can expect if we stabilize the environment also on the interest rate for the collection as well as the expected direction where we are going with the contribution of the P&C. Don't forget that this year we were in any case having a bad natural catastrophe year.
We do put in the capital generation only the current year, contrary to, I know, the norm maybe in the market. We are quite more conservative. I think that the EUR 4.5 billion is really a lower end level on to which projecting going forward. The beat was also given by good financial segment result, where we have different topics, including our financial holdings of the asset management, wealth management, but including also a positive development in some business treated under Solvency I, which is our pension business in France.
Michael Huttner
Insurance Analyst, Berenberg
Brilliant. Thank you very, very much.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Next question, please.

The next question is from Steven Haywood, HSBC. Please go ahead.
Steven Haywood
Analyst, HSBC
Thank you very much. Two questions from me. One is just to clarify on your Solvency II position at the start of the year. Secondly, can you give us an indication on what is going on with the Italian government's review of the Natixis deal? Could there be any implications from this as well? Thank you.
Fabio Cleva
Head of Investor and Rating Agency Relations, Generali
Thank you very much, Steven. The first question is for Cristiano, while the second question is for Philippe.
Cristiano Borean
Group CFO, Generali
Hi, Steven. On the 7 March 2024, we published in our slide commentary, 214% Solvency II ratio, expected. By the way, if I look at the sensitivity between the 7 March 2024 and these recent days, there are no material change because there are ups and downs in various pieces. Here, we are embedding already some regulatory changes like the EIOPA curves and the effect of the Intermonte deal on Banca Generali.
